result.subject: Re: UAT sign-off - core replenishment
result.body:
The January 2025 sign-off does not support describing it as acceptance of the whole programme. The signed text states: "This sign-off does not extend to fresh categories, which remain in scope for a later phase, and does not constitute acceptance of the overall programme." The sign-off covers user acceptance testing for core replenishment for the 25 store pilot cohort, covering ambient and dry goods categories. [1]

Lena Fischer confirmed the wording at the time, writing: "Signed and attached. The wording is what I asked for, thank you for being careful with it." [2]

At the UAT readiness review on 21 January 2025, Lena Fischer stated the scope she was signing: "I am signing that ambiant core replenishment works for twenty-five stores, not that the project is finished." [3] [4]

Fresh categories were not accepted in January 2025. The fresh Phase 2 go/no-go decision was taken on 17 November 2025, when Lena Fischer stated: "Then that is my decision. Go live on produce, dairy and chilled ready meals. Bakery comes later as its own thing." [5] [6]

Recommendation: describe the January 2025 sign-off in the steering pack as acceptance of core replenishment UAT for the 25 store pilot cohort, covering ambient and dry goods, with fresh categories explicitly excluded and no acceptance of the overall programme. This follows from the signed wording, Lena Fischer's confirmation of that wording, and the later fresh go/no-go decision on 17 November 2025. [1] [2] [5] [6]

results.name: Updated morning brief cites new scheduling evidence

result.text:
Ana Duarte's delivered message of 6 July 2026 schedules the bakery evidence review for Thursday 9 July 2026 at 10:00 Helsinki time, commits to preparing the comparison of prepared extracts and a separate environment including the earlier access decision and setup estimate, and asks Priya Nair to bring updated requirements from Acme and Nadia Haddad to bring the current integration questions. The meeting request supplied for this brief, however, lists the Acme project check-in for Wednesday 8 July 2026 at 10:00 (+03:00) with attendees Ana Duarte, Priya Nair and Nadia Haddad and the purpose of reviewing bakery integration, prepared extracts and outstanding Acme decisions. The two dates conflict, so the correct slot should be confirmed before invites go out. [1]

On access, Priya Nair ruled out direct read access for Meridian, writing "Extracts. Slower is acceptable, the other thing is not." (2 March 2026), and Tomas Lindholm estimated on 26 February 2026 that a separate environment would take "Roughly two weeks of setup and it needs somewhere to run," with extracts as the cheaper option. These are the access decision and setup estimate Ana's 6 July message says she will include in her preparation. [2] [3] [1]

Unresolved: extract versus till reconciliation. At the Q2 business review on 16 June 2026, Nadia Haddad reported that she had put the extract totals next to the till numbers for January to March and that "They do not reconcile. The extract is lower." She declined to give a number in the meeting because she had had the figures for two days and did not trust them yet, saying "It is not a rounding difference." Robert Kahn asked "Lower by how much?" No answer or follow-up date appears in the supplied records. The draft's claim that the 3.4% board figure is derived from those totals is not supported by any supplied passage and should be removed, as is the draft's paraphrase of Robert demanding an answer "before the next one, not after" and Marco saying "We will come back on it" — neither quote appears in the supplied turns. [4] [5] [6] [7] [8] [9] [10]

Unresolved: erasure request. At the same 16 June 2026 review, Ana Duarte opened the item by noting Sofia raised a request in November to have a personal detail removed from documentation, and Marco Rossi reported "Still not fully closed. Three of four locations done. The fourth... is a document version." The supplied records do not show Robert Kahn saying "Then close it" — that quote is unsupported and should be removed. Separately, on 21 November 2025 Ana Duarte wrote that the old version remained in the document history on the project site, which she could not delete herself, and that she had raised it with IT; no completion is recorded since. Per the request, the specific personal detail is not repeated here. [11] [12] [13] [14] [15]

Decision needed: chain-wide numbers and the warehouse field. On 17 June 2026 Robert Kahn asked Marco for a chain-wide number before the end of the month, "because our budget cycle starts in August and if this is not in it, it does not happen until 2028." Marco sent indicative figures on 26 June 2026: chain wide for the three fresh categories across 340 stores, additional annual licence of approximately 420 thousand plus implementation of approximately 260 thousand one off. In the same message he stated in writing that the value case depended on a data field identified as a dependency in April 2024 and never obtained, and that without it chain wide will reduce waste by less than the pilot suggests. On 29 June 2026 Lena Fischer identified the owner as Nils Ackermann under logistics IT, noting Priya had asked him twice, in 2024 and again in 2025, and Robert replied "Then I will ask him." No reply from Robert resolving the field is recorded, and the end-of-June deadline has passed. [16] [17] [18] [19]

Correction to carry into the approval summary: the signed UAT wording of 21 January 2025 states the sign-off "does not extend to fresh categories, which remain in scope for a later phase, and does not constitute acceptance of the overall programme." The draft attributes to Ana's 6 July delivered message a claim that she described the January 2025 UAT sign-off as acceptance of the whole programme including fresh. The supplied 6 July delivered message (X505d0adac1) contains no such statement — it concerns only the bakery review scheduling. The correction item therefore lacks support in the supplied passages and should be removed or held until the message making that claim is supplied. [20] [1]

Watch item: DC-2 feed reliability. On 10 February 2026 Ivan Petrov wrote "We will build assuming roughly fortnightly failures," and advised ignoring the comment about the scheduled job. The draft's claims that four of January's fourteen failures correlated with a scheduled job, that Priya has twice said the job does not exist, and that this was flagged internally but not raised with Priya are not supported by the supplied passages and should be removed. What is supported: the fortnightly-failure planning assumption and Ivan's advice to disregard the scheduled-job comment. [21]

Recommendation: before the bakery check-in, (a) confirm with Ana, Priya and Nadia whether the meeting is Wednesday 8 July or Thursday 9 July at 10:00, since the calendar request and Ana's 6 July scheduling message conflict; (b) chase a date for the extract-versus-till reconciliation answer last raised 16 June 2026, where Robert's "Lower by how much?" remains unanswered; and (c) confirm whether Robert has approached Nils Ackermann about the warehouse goods-receipt field, given the end-of-June deadline has passed and the chain-wide value case depends on it. These follow directly from the scheduling conflict, the unanswered QBR question, and the recorded ownership exchange of 29 June 2026. [1] [8] [9] [10] [18] [19] [17]

result.text:
Robert Kahn's central and consistent priority is fresh waste reduction with return on investment inside twelve months. At the March 2024 solution demo he said: "Whatever we sign, I need return on investment inside twelve months. Ambient efficiency is nice. I understand it is real. But the board cares about waste, because waste is what was in the newspaper, so that is what the case has to be built on." He tied phase two to that clock, saying "then phase two needs to be inside the twelve months, kind of like does it not," and called it "the only constraint I have." [1] [2] [3] [4] [5]

At the June 2024 commercial and SOW review he asked that the value case be written down as fresh waste reduction with ROI inside twelve months of signature, so that "in fourteen months nobody can tell me the project was a success because ambient inventory improved." At the same meeting he asked for the quarterly review to be put in the SOW, "Not as a nice idea, basically as an obligation." [6] [7] [8] [9] [10] [11] [12]

At the May 2025 90-day post-go-live business review he repeated: "I did not approve a project to reduce ambiant ambiant inventory. Ambient inventory was fine. I approved a project because we are throwing away food and it was in newspaper." At the same meeting, after Lena Fischer reported that planners do not trust the morning numbers, "which undoes the thing we bought," he called it "the most concerning sentence in this meeting." [13] [14] [15] [16] [17] [18] [19]

At the June 2025 steering committee he said "I am being consistent. Since March last year I have said one thing," pressing for a fresh go-live date, and demanded a baseline be agreed in writing before go-live: "Then agree one before go-live and not after, because after go live everybody's baseline is the one that makes them look good." [20] [21] [22] [23] [24]

He reacts well to directness. At the June 2026 Q2 quarterly business review, when Marco Rossi confirmed the twelve-month ROI was missed ("On that reading, no," after Robert observed "So the answer is no"), Robert pressed "Is there another reading?" In a June 2026 email he wrote: "I asked yesterday whether we got return on investment inside twelve months and you said no. I appreciated that." He valued Marco's June 2026 written explanation of why the twelve-month expectation was missed, calling it "the most useful email I have had from a supplier this year," and immediately asked Lena Fischer "who owns the warehouse system?" [25] [26] [27] [28] [29]

He reacts sharply to numbers that cannot be trusted. On learning at the Q2 2026 review that the extract and till data do not reconcile, he said: "I took three point four to the board in April. Then I would like to know whether I was wrong, and I would like to know it before the next one, not after." Lena Fischer noted "We both did." Nadia Haddad responded that she did not have a cause yet and Marco Rossi said "We will come back on it." [30] [31] [32] [33] [34] [35]

On process he wants brevity: at the March 2024 demo he said "Thank you. Send me one page, not forty." [36]

On chain-wide scaling, Marco Rossi's June 2026 email gave the honest caveat: "If it is not resolved, chain wide will reduce waste by less than the pilot suggests, because the slow moving articles are a larger share of the tail across 340 stores than across 25." The email also stated the twelve-month expectation was missed because the value case depended on fresh, which depended on a data field identified as a dependency in April 2024 and never obtained. Lena Fischer identified the warehouse system owner as Nils Ackermann, under logistics IT, whom Priya has asked twice, in 2024 and again in 2025. Robert asked for the chain-wide number before the end of June 2026 because the budget cycle starts in August and otherwise it does not happen until 2028. [37] [38] [28]

Recommendation: Lead the next conversation with the fresh waste number against the target and the reconciliation answer Nadia owes, since Robert said he wants to know whether the 3.4 board figure was wrong before the next board cycle. [30] [32] [33] [34] [35]

Recommendation: Bring the warehouse-system ownership answer (Nils Ackermann, per Lena Fischer) as a concrete next step, because Robert personally took that question on after Marco's email. [29] [38]

Recommendation: Present chain-wide numbers with the honest caveat Marco already gave him about the slow-moving tail across 340 stores versus 25, and explain why the next number will be different, since Robert wrote that "it will be better this time" is not an answer for the board. [37] [28]

Recommendation: Keep it to one page and put dates, not scopes, in any proposal, consistent with his one-page instruction and his demand for a fresh go-live date and a baseline agreed before go-live. [36] [20] [22]

Evidence gap: Robert's current view of the reconciliation issue is not recorded beyond the June 2026 meeting, and his reaction to any July evidence review is unknown.

citations.quote:
Robert,

Indicative numbers attached. Summary here so you have it in the mail.

Chain wide for the three fresh categories, 340 stores: additional annual licence of
approximately 420 thousand, plus implementation of approximately 260 thousand one off.

On your second point, and this is the honest version.

The twelve month expectation was missed for one reason above all others. The value case
depended on fresh, and fresh depended on a data field that we identified as a dependency
in April 2024 and never obtained. Everything else largely went to plan. We built a
workaround in September 2025 which works acceptably on fast moving articles and poorly on
slow moving ones, and your category manager has been compensating for the difference by
hand ever since.

For the next number to be different, that field has to be available. It is not a RELEX
deliverable and I cannot commit to it on your behalf, which is why I am putting it in
writing rather than in a slide.

If it is not resolved, chain wide will reduce waste by less than the pilot suggests,
because the slow moving articles are a larger share of the tail across 340 stores than
across 25.

Marco Rossi

result.question: Prepare stakeholder guidance for Robert Kahn: observed priorities and reactions, followed by clearly labelled recommendations for the next conversation.
trace: Read 2976 permitted source records at L3.
Verified ROI and waste priorities across demo, SOW review, 90-day review and steering transcripts, including fragmented utterances
Verified reactions to directness (Q2 QBR admission, June 2026 email) and data trust issues (reconciliation, DC-2 planners)
Verified process preferences: one page, quarterly review as obligation, baseline in writing before go-live
Verified chain-wide caveat, warehouse ownership (Nils Ackermann) and budget-cycle timing in permitted email records
Confirmed no support in supplied passages for a 2.8 target, a July proposal date requirement, or Ana Duarte declining to scale cohort figures; removed or qualified accordingly
Verified 38 quoted passages against runtime sources.
